issues.legal_issue: The statutory limit on interest for an outstanding mortgage liability does not authorize reopening completed accounts to credit interest already paid, within the contractual rate, against principal.
material_facts: The mortgage bond provided for compound interest at nine per cent per annum.
Some payments were made before the mortgage suit was filed, including payments of interest at a rate above five per cent simple but within the contractual rate.
The mortgagee later claimed the remaining liability before the officer dealing with the separation of interests in composite property.
issues.conclusion: The accounts could not be reopened to apply pre-suit interest payments above five per cent simple, but within the contractual rate, toward reducing principal.
issues.legal_principle: Section 9(1) of the Evacuee Interest (Separation) Act, 1951 limits the interest chargeable against the mortgaged property on liability still due; it does not authorize reopening past accounts or recharacterizing interest already paid as principal repayment. Section 3 gives the Act overriding effect, but the Court found no provision authorizing the proposed account reopening. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: mortgage_claim_in_composite_property and prior_interest_payments_made and prior_interest_exceeded_simple_cap and prior_interest_within_contract_rate

predicates.mortgage_claim_in_composite_property: A mortgagee made a claim for outstanding mortgage liability in a proceeding to separate interests in property that included an evacuee's interest.
predicates.prior_interest_payments_made: The mortgagor or another liable person made interest payments before the mortgage suit was filed.
predicates.prior_interest_exceeded_simple_cap: The pre-suit interest payments were at a rate above the applicable simple-interest limit.
predicates.prior_interest_within_contract_rate: The pre-suit interest payments did not exceed the rate permitted by the mortgage contract.

issues.definition: When a mortgagee claims outstanding liability in a proceeding concerning composite property and pre-suit interest was paid above the simple-interest limit but within the contract rate, that excess is not credited against principal.

issues.legal_issue: When an outstanding mortgage liability is governed by a civil decree, interest from the filing of the suit must be calculated at the applicable simple-interest limit, and payments made after suit must be applied first to that interest and then to principal.
material_facts: A civil court had entered a mortgage decree that was binding on the officer, subject to the statutory interest limit.
The mortgage suit was filed before the relevant account was determined in the proceeding concerning composite property.
Payments were made after the suit was filed, and the mortgagee also claimed the costs awarded in the suit.
issues.conclusion: The outstanding liability had to be recalculated using simple interest at five per cent per annum on principal from the suit date; post-suit payments had to be applied first to interest and any excess to principal. The awarded costs were recoverable without interest.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 8(3), a civil decree is binding on the Competent Officer subject to sections 9 and 10. Section 9(1) therefore requires the officer to apply the simple-interest limit when determining the liability still due, notwithstanding the decree. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.mortgage_claim_in_composite_property: A mortgagee made a claim for outstanding mortgage liability in a proceeding to separate interests in property that included an evacuee's interest.
predicates.mortgage_decree_exists: A civil court had entered a decree determining liability under the mortgage.
predicates.payments_made_after_suit: Payments toward the mortgage liability were made after the mortgage suit was filed.

issues.definition: When a mortgagee makes a claim in a composite-property proceeding, a civil mortgage decree exists, and payments were made after suit, the post-suit liability is calculated at the simple-interest limit, with those payments applied first to interest and then to principal.
